author: TEDx Talks
description:
Why do the world’s most dangerous actors invest in children – while democracies don’t?
In this urgent and eye-opening talk, Sofie Lilli Stoffel explores the overlooked link between childhood, resilience, and national security. Drawing on neuroscience, research, and global case studies she shows how protecting children today helps determine the societies we will live in tomorrow.
Planning for the future means treating childhood as a strategic priority, not an afterthought. 

Sofie Lilli Stoffel is a security researcher examining how early-life experiences shape cycles of violence, societal resilience, and the long-term stability of democracies. She is a Research Fellow at the Global Public Policy Institute in Berlin, a former McCloy Fellow at the Harvard Kennedy School, and co-founder of the Women in Foreign Affairs Network.

She studied international relations, public policy, psychology, and negotiation sciences at Harvard University, the Australian National University, and Maastricht
title: Why extremist groups target young people | Sofie Lilli Stoffel | TEDxBerlin Salon
